title: Why? #4 remade: the angle keeps turning, sin²θ + cos²θ is…? (predict-first, Remotion, lofi, 22 s)

The angle keeps turning. sin²θ + cos²θ is… A 1 · B θ · C varies
Comment your guess before you watch 👇

Why? #4. Put a point on a circle of radius 1. Its height is sin θ, its width is cos θ, and Pythagoras on that triangle gives sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 → A.
Spin the point: sin²θ and cos²θ trade places, one grows while the other shrinks, and the total never moves.

NDA 2025 (I) asked it (Maths Q35): p = sin α − sin(α − 90°). Maximum value of p?
sin(α − 90°) = −cos α, so p = sin α + cos α. Square it: p² = sin²α + cos²α + 2 sin α cos α = 1 + sin 2α ≤ 2 → p ≤ √2 → (b).
Trap: (d) 2 needs sin and cos to be 1 at the same time.
